This Miscellaneous Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act has been filed at the instance of the Insurance Company challenging the impugned award dated 17/03/2008 passed by the Fourth Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Fast Track), District Dabra District Gwalior (M.P.) in Claim Case No.55/2007, whereby the Claims Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.25,800/- in favour of the claimant and directed the Insurance Company to pay the compensation to the claimant and thereafter recover the same from the owner and driver of the offending vehicle.
2. Brief facts of the case is that claimant filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act claiming compensation to tune of Rs. 50,00,000/- for the injuries said to have been caused due to alleged accident occurred on 08/02/2007 while claimant-Seema was travelling on tractor NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:28324 2 MA-610-2008 bearing registration No.
MP07-H-8901 alongwith other occupants and other relatives and tractor trolley turned turtle due to rash and negligent driving of respondent No.2, as a result of which Ramesh and Pushpa died and other occupants and respondent No.1/claimant were injured.

entities.text: Fourth Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Fast Track), District Dabra District Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The aforesaid tractor was said to be owned by respondent No.3 and 4 and insured with appellant.
Respondent Nos. 2, 3, 4 and appellant filed their written statement denying all the allegations.

Appellant/Insurance Company contended that tractor was insured for agricultural purposes and at the time of accident, it was used for The New India Assurance Co.Ltd. vs Smt. Seema on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199973023/
1 carrying passenger.

sentences.text: Therefore, it breached terms and conditions of insurance policy.

Hence,
Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation to the claimant.

3. Tribunal framed the issues and after taking evidence of both the parties, awarded compensation in favour of claimant/ respondent No. 1 with interest of filing of claim petition till its realization.

4. Appellant/Insurance Company filed this appeal on the ground that offending vehicle was insured for agricultural purposes and at the time of accident, it was used for carrying passengers alongwith claimant.
Therefore, it is violation of terms and conditions of insurance policy and in passing impugned Award, Tribunal also found that Tractor was used for commercial purpose for carrying passenger on rent.
It is submitted that Insurance Company did not receive any premium for passengers who were travelling in tractor.
So, it is totally breach of terms and conditions of insurance policy and Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:28324 3 MA-610-2008 to the claimant.

It is further submitted that claimant was not third party, therefore, findings of the Tribunal that Insurance Company shall pay compensation to the claimants with liberty to recover from owner and driver is erroneous and accordingly, it is prayed that the Insurance Company be exonerated from the liability to pay compensation to the claimants.
5. No one appeared on behalf owner and driver of the offending vehicle despite service of notice.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the entire record.
7.

In para 10 of the impugned Award, Tribunal hold that claimant was sitting on the tractor and tractor was insured for agricultural purposes but at the time of accident, tractor was being used for carrying passengers not for agricultural purposes.
Therefore, it is breach of terms and conditions of insurance policy and no objection was filed by owner and driver of the offending vehicle against this finding.
The findings of the Tribunal in this regard is intact, as it was not challenged by owner and driver of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the findings of the Tribunal that owner and driver breached terms and conditions of insurance policy is correct in the eye of law, and is hereby affirmed.

8. Now the only issue is as to whether, the insurance company should be directed to pay the amounts and then recover it from the owner, which measure this Court adopted in various cases to avoid hardship to the claimants.

9. A reading of Manager, National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Saju P. Paul and anr (2013) 2 SCC 41 wherein the Apex Court held that it would indicate NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:28324 4 MA-610-2008 that therein the injured/claimant was travelling in a vehicle as a spare driver, as contended by the claimant himself.

sentences.text: In considering the measure of pay and recover, in Saju P. Paul (supra), the Apex Court held that noticed a number of decisions where such measure was employed.

National Insurance Co. Ltd. v.
Baljit Kaur, (2004) 2 SCC 1 , wherein the Apex Court held that it was a case in which the Tribunal and the this Court proceeded in terms of the decisions of the Apex Court in New India Assurance Company v. Satpal Singh (2000) 1 SCC 237 , wherein the Apex Court held that it was overruled in New India Asurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Asha Rani, (2003) 2 SCC 223.

sentences.text: Since the Tribunal and the High Court had allowed the compensation based on Satpal Singh (supra) , the measure of pay and recover was adopted in the said case.
National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Challa Bharathamma (2004) 8 SCC 517 wherein the Apex Court held that it is yet another case in which 'pay and recover' was ordered.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therein the breach of condition of policy was projected insofar as the vehicle having not been covered by a permit to ply for hire or reward.
The finding of the High Court as to the absence of permit not leading to violation of policy condition, was reversed by this Court.
Therein also the measure of pay and recover was adopted.

11. National Insurance Company Limited v. Kaushalaya Devi , (2008) 8 SCC 246 wherein the Apex Court held that it was a case in which an identical condition of gratuitous passenger being carried in a good carriage vehicle had NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:28324 5 MA-610-2008 resulted in the liability being mulcted on the owner and the insurer absolved of its liability to indemnify.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Kaushalaya Devi , (2008) 8 SCC 246
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therein it was directed that the amount deposited by the insurer if withdrawn, it would be recovered from the owner and if not returned, it would be refunded to the insurance company,
and the claimants would be entitled to proceed against the owner for recovery of the award amounts.
12.

This is a case in which there was a fundamental breach noticed and the deceased claimant, being a person who travelled in the goods carriage after paying fare, the damages for his death was not entitled to be indemnified by the insurer.
There was no amount deposited or paid by the insurance company.
In the above circumstances, we find absolutely no reason to interfere with the order of the High Court 13.

In the present case, according to pleading claimant was travelling on the tractor as a passenger and tractor was used for carrying passengers, not for agricultural purposes and Insurance Company has not taken any premium for passengers.
Therefore, Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation.
The finding of the Tribunal that Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation to the claimant with liberty to recover from owner and driver is not correct in the eye of law.
14. Accordingly, the findings of the Claims Tribunal on this issue are modified.
The Insurance Company is hereby totally exonerated from liability to pay compensation to the claimant.
The claimant is entitled to recover the awarded compensation amount from the owner and driver of the offending vehicle jointly and severally.

In view of the above,
miscellaneous appeal filed by the appellants/ Insurance Company stands disposed of.
